newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks rebound on bottom-fishers, Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks rebound on bottom-fishers, Brazil.

text.p: Mexican stocks reversed their early slide and were heading upwards for the pyschological 5,100-barrier in midday trading on Monday.
Dealers said share prices gained after bargain-hunters stepped in, taking refuge from volatile equity markets in Brazil.
"We're seeing Latam funds flowing into Mexico rather than Brazil, which still has problems, as prices look good here," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index was up 26.21 points, or 0.52 percent, at 5,093.24.
In Sao Paulo, the Bovespa index of most traded stocks was down 1.96 percent to 12,019 points.
Dealers said that volume was much thinner than for many recent sessions; thus light buying by stockpickers had an exaggerated impact on the market.
"There's hardly any shouting on the floor; it's very quiet down here. It rebounded because a few stocks had reached rock-bottom," another floor trader said.
Financial firm Bancomer A's shares were the most active, accounting for more than one-quarter of a slow total volume of 46.9 million shares traded.
